name: Systems Architecture
summary: The decisions that determine whether a system grows or seizes up — the shape, the data across it, the patterns that keep it standing when a part fails, and how to communicate all three.
prerequisites: Requires Docker and back-end experience: this course decides between designs, it does not teach a language.
syllabus: Monolith, microservices, SOA, serverless and service mesh
The twelve factors of modern applications
Data across services: CAP, consistency, replication and sharding
Asynchronous messaging with Kafka and RabbitMQ
Resilience patterns: circuit breaker, retry, bulkhead and throttling
Cloud design patterns: CQRS, event sourcing, saga and the strangler fig
Search, real time, and documenting the decisions you made
topics: Monolith: when it is still the right call
Microservices: boundaries, communication and operational cost
SOA, serverless and service mesh
The twelve factors of modern applications
Synchronous and asynchronous communication between services
Messaging: Kafka, RabbitMQ and managed queues
Guaranteed delivery, idempotency and message ordering
The CAP theorem, and choosing between consistency and availability
Eventual consistency, and the user who sees the old value
Replication, sharding, and the query that no longer fits
Circuit breaker, retry with backoff, and the retry storm
Bulkhead, throttling and back pressure
CQRS and event sourcing: reading and writing through different models
Saga and compensating transactions, where there is no distributed commit
Strangler fig, sidecar and ambassador: changing a system that is running
Performance antipatterns: chatty I/O, extraneous fetching, the busy database
Search engines: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and Solr
Real time: WebSockets, Server-Sent Events and long polling
Service registry, discovery and API gateway
Recording architectural decisions (ADRs) and defending them
